scene mollyamitrain1
But at least we have legs to look at for now.

And all we can do is hope that Ami winds up in the same position her uncle/father did a while back where she gets to pseudo-molest Molly from behind on a crowded train while fulfilling another one of the Irish girl’s fantasies.
: You know...it wasn’t all that long ago that I almost fulfilled a lifelong fantasy of mine with your dad on this very train route.
Oh. I guess she’s just saying it.
: Lucky. Cause, if it’s the fantasy I’m thinking of, I have the same exact one.
: I think I heard a while ago that most girls fantasize about that at least once.
: Are you sure you didn’t hear that most girls experience it at least once?
: I hope not. That’s much less fun and way more sad for those who aren’t as depraved as us.
scene mollyamitrain2
: Speaking of things that are both sad and fun, though, I had a good time today. We don’t hang out as much as we should.
: I concur. What about this is sad, though?
: The fact that you’ll forever feel like an outcast despite this being your home country now and how you’ve grown so accustomed to being ostracized that you’ve stopped reacting to it altogether.
scene mollyamitrain3
: Oh. Well, yes. It is sad when you put it like that. But I’ve had plenty of time to get used to being an outcast, so...
: I get it. I’m also an outcast, Molly. I’m sure everybody would be looking at me differently if they knew I willingly have sex with my dad.
: Ahem.
scene mollyamitrain4
: Hi. I’m Ami. I have sex with my dad.
: As proud as I am to see you unabashedly proclaiming your love for interests that other people would surely look down on, I do think telling strangers about that might be taking it a step too far.
: Wooooooow. Nihongo jouzu desu ne.
scene mollyamitrain5
: I think I’m just going to stop talking forever.
: But talking is what makes you you! Just try to look at the bright side and...be happy about how many people have complimented your speaking today?
: They’d be reacting the same way if I just said “thank you.”
scene mollyamitrain6
: What can I say? We’re easy to impress and not afraid to hand out compliments.
: The best compliment of all is the lack thereof. That’s why I like hanging out with all of you guys so much. It feels like you’ve actually accepted me.
scene mollyamitrain7
: It shouldn’t just feel like it. We have accepted you. In fact, we kind of need you.

: Without Molly MacCormack, the manga club would fall apart. The rest of us aren’t nearly as good at sewing. Plus, I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve used your characters as supports in gacha games.

: You’re an invaluable part of our friend group. And you should take solace in the fact that, if anyone was going to be kicked out of it, it would be me. Nobody in their right mind is voting you out first.
: I do have fewer death threats under my belt. At least those not shrouded in delusions of grandeur pertaining to assorted virtual worlds.
scene mollyamitrain8
: I don’t think anyone wants you gone either, though. At least no one in the manga club.
: I don’t know about that. Yasu’s seemed pretty scared of me lately.

: Yasu was deathly afraid of the closet for a solid month as well when she thought she heard “the void” inside of it. I think we can write her fears off as mostly nonsensical. Except for when they aren’t.
: Just write everybody off except for us. I got a lot happier when I stopped caring about the world outside of school and home.
: Now, I can tell any random person I see about all the sex I have with my dad and nothing ever changes. Isn’t that great?
scene mollyamitrain9
: Do you ever wish things would change, though?
: Like what?
: Like...say you’re playing a game. And you’re having a lot of fun with it.
: But then one day, all of a sudden, you feel like starting over before you’ve even finished.
: Maybe you got to a part that was too difficult. Or maybe you’re just not liking how you built your character or something.
: So you make an alt...or start a new save file...and do things a little differently than you did last time just to see what it’s like.
: I feel like that sometimes. Like what I’ve been doing isn’t really what I want to do even though it probably is or I wouldn’t have done it at all. You know?
: Yeah, I think I get what you mean. I feel like that sometimes too.
scene black
: It’s still the same game at the end of the day, though.
: And even if there are multiple endings, most of what you see is going to be the same.
: That said, I think it’s more important to see the ending before you do something as dramatic as starting a new save file. Unless you’re one of those people who’s just afraid to ever end things.
: Besides, there are too many games out there to keep playing the same one.
: The hard part is actually finding them.
scene mollyamitrain10
Whether there was a double meaning or not to what Ami Arakawa was saying didn’t really matter. The words still resonated with Molly either way.

This life and way of living were all she’d ever known. But even though it was the path she chose, it still felt, more often than not, that she’d unintentionally locked herself out of a ton of content.
In fact, in some alternate universe, even this was probably missable. But if it was, would it even be because of her? Or would it be the result of something else?
Is there anything she can do at this point to change her fate? Or have the route and its ending already been written?
There’s no way to know but waiting it out.
Or rather, there is.
She just doesn’t know about it yet.
: Do you ever wonder what it’s like to be cool?
: Not really, no.
scene mollyamitrain11
: Me either. I’m glad we’re on the same page.
: You and I are on the same page pretty much all the time. You’re the only person I know who never really had any sort of crazy reaction to finding out I’m an incestuous daughterslut.

: I was desensitized to incest long before I even met you. Your relationship with the Supreme Overlord is but one more example of how the barrier between fiction and reality has dissolved into nothing for me.
: Meaning that you would also have sex with your dad?
scene mollyamitrain12
: That...is not what I meant. No.
: One day, I’m going to find someone who responds positively to that question. Mark my words. I can’t be the only teenage girl out there who understands how hot this is.
scene mollyamitrain13
: Can I ask you something about that, actually?
: Anything. Nobody ever wants to talk to me about it and I have so much to get off of my chest.
: I just want to know if you think there’s a chance you might actually...you know...
: Win.
scene mollyamitrain14
: Why wouldn’t there be?
: There might be. I don’t...really know.
: I have a hard time getting in the heads of other people. You saw how I was with Rin. It’s just tough for me to comprehend what’s...romantically possible at times.
: And even if you and Sir love each other as deeply as it seems you do, you’re still a niche pick in terms of a heroine. A fetish, even. But I don’t mean that in a bad way.
scene mollyamitrain15
: You and I are similar in that regard. Just, for me, there’s a cultural barrier instead of a familial one. One that I don’t understand how to purify or...dispel. Nor do I know if I even can.
: Which is part of why I don’t feel entitled to see him as anything more than what he’s been to me. But you do.
: So is that just an example of my feelings being weaker than yours? Is it an example of me being weak as a whole? Or am I just...right in thinking that my chances are worse than everyone else’s?
: Is this because of the annoying racist lady?
scene mollyamitrain16
: You not being Japanese doesn’t make any difference at all, Molly. And I know it might it feel like it does, but it doesn’t.
: Love is love no matter what shape it takes. And if someone like me can win, which I fully intend to, of course someone like you can win as well.
: I’m sorry if that was an odd question. This is just a...conservative country. And I know that things like this can be frowned upon at times.
: We’re in high school, Molly. I think there are bigger things to be frowned upon than your race.
: So if by some stroke of luck I do take on a bigger role one day...what then?
scene mollyamitrain17
: Will we still be friends? Or will you refuse to accept me? Because that will surely play a role in my decision as well.
: Would it really? You like me that much?

: Of course. You and the rest of the girls in the manga club are the first real friends I’ve ever had. Or at least that’s what my dad would call you since you’re not encased inside of a computer monitor.
: We would still be friends, Molly. Of course we’d still be friends.
scene mollyamitrain18
: I just wouldn’t let that get in the way of me having sex with him and he’d probably cheat on you a whole bunch since me and him are addicted to each other’s bodies.
: Well, if it is an addiction, I suppose it can’t be helped. This seems like a fair enough compromise for me.
scene mollyamitrain19
: It goes both ways too. I don’t mind you coming over to help get him off if I’m ever busy or something. Niki’s the one we’ve gotta look out for. She hates fun.
: Are you getting off here? I still have a few more stops to go meet up with Rin and Futaba.
: Yeah, I’ve got some errands to run before I go try to seduce my dad as a cat.
scene mollyamitrain20
: Let’s do this again, though! I always have fun when it’s just us two.
: I’m free next weekend as well. I’ll be working on the campaign if you want to come over.
scene mollyamitrain21
: It’s a date. I’ll text you later to tell you how Operation: Daughterpussy went.
: Please be mindful of the things you say in crowds. Even I’m not that brazen.
scene mollyamitrain22
: Attention, everyone! My name is Ami Arakawa and I have tons of sex with my dad! So if you ever see me again, please point at me and shout about it! The whole world should know!
: Or...do that.
: I suppose that works too.
scene mollyamitrain23
: A date, huh?...
scene black
: Should I wear my dress again?
Whether there was a different meaning or not to what Ami Arakawa said didn’t really matter. The words still resonated with Molly either way.
And as her train kept on to its destination, she was glad that she had finally felt seen.
But would these feelings spiral the same ways they did the last time she thought a classmate saw her?
This was one more thing she’d struggle to wrap her head around.
Fortunately, she’d be able to turn it off once she made it back home.
And as she crawled beneath the covers, letting the glow of her cell phone illuminate the shallow depths of the tiny fortress she had built to hide from her sleeping roommate, her lips parted.
Her legs spread.
And shallow breaths escaped her while her hand danced beneath her shorts.
All to the tune of a red-headed catgirl and a picture of her latest misdeed.
